extracted.intended_audience: educated early-18th-century English readers — especially poets, essay-readers, and unmarried persons choosing a spouse
extracted.subtask_description: A set of prescriptive essayistic rules and social guidance from The Spectator (early 18th century) about poetic practice (use of classical mythology, genre-appropriateness, truth in thought), coffee-house manners and listening, and criteria for choosing a marriage partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward vehement narrations / public report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Force of the Expression lies very often more in the Look, the Tone of Voice, or the Gesture, than the Words themselves; which being repeated in any other Manner by the Undiscerning, bear a very different Interpretation from their original Meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept authoritative, vehement narrations at face value — consider other possible ways events might have occurred rather than fixing on the teller's single settled version. The writer describes a tactic of disputing a narrator's single stated outcome by insisting on the many other possibilities, thereby exposing exaggeration or falsehood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posture of attention in a coffee-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Good Breeding obliges a Man to maintain the Figure of the keenest Attention; the true Posture of which in a Coffee-house I take to consist in leaning over a Table, with the Edge of it pressing hard upon your Stomach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To appear attentive and polite in public conversation, adopt a posture (leaning forward, appearing pained by the narration) that signals keen interest. The more 'pain' you display, the more gracious the bending, and narrators assume you forget bodily discomfort through pleasure of hearing — i.e., this posture encourages and flatters the speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of liars (embellishers vs reciters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of these Liars there are two Sorts. The Genius of the first consists in much Impudence and a strong Memory; the others have added to these Qualifications a good Understanding and smooth Language. These therefore have only certain Heads...and may be call'd Embellishers; the others repeat only what they hear...and are called Reciters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating reported news or gossip, recognize whether the teller is (a) an embellisher who invents or refines narratives with eloquence and false particulars, or (b) a reciter who mechanically repeats what he heard. Embellishers may be more plausible but more fabricated; reciters spread error purely by repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never tell thy dreams (Epictetus' precept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Never tell thy Dreams, says that Philosopher, for tho' thou thy self may'st take a Pleasure in telling thy Dream, another will take no Pleasure in hearing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule for correspondents and writers of visions/dreams: avoid publishing or relating dreams casually — audiences rarely care, and publication risks overloading a periodical with visions of varied quality. Use restraint and apply allowances for age/condition if publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for beautiful/thoughtful writing: truth and justice
rubrics_metrics.description: No Thought is beautiful which is not just, and no Thought can be just which is not founded in Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate (and compose) poetry and serious writing by whether ideas are just and grounded in truth; aesthetic beauty depends on moral/epistemic rightness rather than mere ornament or classical allusion detached from fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pagan mythology in serious panegyrics or poems on real events
rubrics_metrics.description: I do hereby strictly require every Person, who shall write on this Subject, to remember that he is a Christian, and not to Sacrifice his Catechism to his Poetry...I do expect of him in the first place, to make his own Poem, without depending upon Phoebus...I do likewise positively forbid the sending of Mercury with any particular Message...I do further declare, that I shall not allow the Destinies to have had an hand in the Deaths of the several thousands who have been slain...I do therefore strictly forbid the Fates to cut the Thread of Man's Life upon any pretence whatsoever, unless it be for the sake of the Rhyme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing serious, contemporary panegyrics or poems on public events (e.g., a prospect of peace), do not invoke classical gods or mythological agents as literal causal forces or personified actors. Restrict pagan figures to metaphor, simile, or very short allusion; avoid treating ancient deities as if they shaped recent history. (Exception noted for female poets' freedom in the essay.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of classical mythology permitted in mock-heroic poems
rubrics_metrics.description: In Mock-Heroick Poems, the Use of the Heathen Mythology is not only excusable but graceful, because it is the Design of such Compositions to divert, by adapting the fabulous Machines of the Ancients to low Subjects...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre matters: mock-heroic poems intentionally employ and parody ancient machinery — classical gods and fables are appropriate here to produce wit and ridicule. Allow mythological apparatus when the intent is burlesque or satirical, not when the subject is serious and contemporary.

rubrics_metrics.name: In pastorals, favour local superstition over antiquated classical fables
rubrics_metrics.description: He has given a new Life, and a more natural Beauty to this way of Writing by substituting in the place of these Antiquated Fables, the superstitious Mythology which prevails among the Shepherds of our own Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pastoral poetry, use contemporary/local rural beliefs and superstitions rather than imported Pagan mythology to achieve naturalness and authenticity. This substitution can refresh the genre and make descriptions more believable and vivid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal qualities to value in choosing a marriage partner
rubrics_metrics.description: A virtuous Disposition, a good Understanding, an agreeable Person, and an easy Fortune, are the things which should be chiefly regarded on this Occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating suitors, prioritize moral character, intelligence, pleasant disposition, and moderate financial security. Prefer a man of excellent talents and moderate estate to a man whose chief recommendation is wealth, because good faculties can earn riches but riches cannot buy worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid men of wit who are addicted to town pleasures
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many ingenious Men, whose Abilities do little else but make themselves and those about them uneasy: Such are those who are far gone in the Pleasures of the Town, who cannot support Life without quick Sensations and gay Reflections...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn against suitors whose wit is allied to restless appetite for novelty and pleasures of town life; they become sated with possession, will seek new beauties, and are unlikely to provide stable domestic happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a man of sense combined with good-nature and honour
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a sort of Man of Wit and Sense, that can reflect upon his own Make, and that of his Partner, with the Eyes of Reason and Honour...there are those who think themselves bound to supply with Good-nature the Failings of those who love them...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a partner who pairs intelligence with sobriety, generosity, good-nature, and honour: such a man will cultivate his wife's happiness, improve her mind, make prudent use of fortune for her reputation, and remain grateful and attentive in adversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value imagination and lively conversation in a spouse
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Woman is deliberating with herself whom she shall chuse of many near each other in other Pretensions, certainly he of best Understanding is to be preferr'd...Life hangs heavily in the repeated Conversation of one who has no Imagination...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a prospective spouse's capacity for lively thought and discourse: a partner with imagination and the ability to strike out pleasing subjects will continually vary and enrich domestic life, whereas one without imagination makes life dull and stagnant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style for letters to a wife: simplicity, friendship, constancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship, Tenderness and Constancy, drest in a Simplicity of Expression, recommend themselves by a more native Elegance, than passionate Raptures, extravagant Encomiums, and slavish Adoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing letters to one's wife (or evaluating such expressions), favour plainness infused with sincere friendship, tenderness and constancy rather than overwrought, extravagant praise. Sincere simplicity conveys steadier affection than theatrical adoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage should not be treated as a mere commercial bargain
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not mean that Wit, and a Capacity to entertain, is what should be highly valued, except it is founded upon Good-nature and Humanity...All I hope for is, that the Lady Fair will make use of the first light Night to show B. T. she understands a Marriage is not to be considered as a common Bargain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage treating marriage purely as a transactional arrangement; social and moral commitments (devotion, honour, gratitude) should factor into the choice and conduct of spouses rather than only settlements and legal terms.
